title: Data structures and algorithms core
description: The patterns behind most coding interviews, in an order where each step builds on the last.

nodes.title: Arrays
nodes.summary: Index arithmetic, in-place edits, prefix sums and reading a problem for its real constraint. Almost everything else builds on these.

nodes.title: Strings
nodes.summary: Strings are arrays of characters with extra traps: immutability, encodings, case and punctuation. Practise scanning and comparing.

nodes.title: Hashing
nodes.summary: Trade memory for time: remember what you have seen in a map or set to turn nested loops into one pass.

nodes.title: Two pointers
nodes.summary: Walk two indexes through a sequence, usually from both ends or at different speeds, to avoid checking every pair.

nodes.title: Sorting and intervals
nodes.summary: Sorting first often makes the rest of the problem easy. Learn what to sort by and what the order lets you assume.

nodes.title: Binary search
nodes.summary: Halve the search space whenever you can answer a yes or no question about the middle. Mind the boundaries.

nodes.title: Stacks
nodes.summary: Last in, first out: matching brackets, undoing work and keeping a monotonic list of candidates.

nodes.title: Sliding window
nodes.summary: Keep a window over a sequence and grow or shrink it while maintaining a summary, so each element is handled once.

nodes.title: Greedy choices
nodes.summary: Take the locally best step and prove it is safe. Practise spotting when it works and when it does not.

nodes.title: Dynamic programming
nodes.summary: Define the state, write the recurrence, then store sub-answers. Start top-down with memoisation, then tighten to a table.

nodes.title: Graphs
nodes.summary: Model the problem as nodes and edges, then explore with depth-first or breadth-first search while tracking what you have visited.
